pool.text: Ivan Pokhabov built a winter quarters near the site for gold trading.
Yakov Pokhabov built a small fort nearby the location of the settlement.
Powed peasants lived here with their wives and children according to historical documents.
The ostrog gained official town rights from the government in the region.
The stone building of the Savior Church was laid in the fort.
Small town became the administrative center of the vast Irkutsk province.
The Siberian Route road connection was built and benefited the town economy.
Siberia was administratively divided at the Yenisei River as part of reforms.
Four leaders of the Polish Baikal Insurrection were executed in the city.
A fire burned out of control destroying the palace and administrative offices.
The city quickly rebounded from the fire and installed electricity.
The first theater was built in the city.
A major train station opened in the city.
Aleksandr Kolchak was executed in the city.
The largest aviation industrial association was set up in the Transbaykal region.
The large Irkutsk Reservoir was built on the Angara River.
The Aleksandr Kolchak monument designed by Vyacheslav Klykov was unveiled.
Seventy-four people died in the city in a mass methanol poisoning incident.
The BBC reported that men in the city had a short average life span.
Armed officers assaulted and tortured two couples during a round up.
